title: Same Operation, Different Permission: Evaluating Whether Guardrails Honor Authorization
abstract: arXiv:2610.16838v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As language-model agents write code, move money and change records on behalf of users, deciding whether an action is authorized has become a central safety problem. Guardrails are often placed in front of these actions, yet few evaluations ask whether their decisions follow authorization: blocking unauthorized actions while still allowing the same actions under valid permission. We introduce \bench{}, a benchmark that contrasts authorization evidence for the same operation in its language track. It combines expert-annotated natural-language scenarios with executed and verified operations, plus externally sourced native-policy requests. \bench{} checks each decision for correctness, usability and resulting effect, and tracks each request across guardrail changes. Our experiments show that many blocked operations stem from failed reviews, not correct denials. Repairing the output format restores usable decisions but changes which authorize

translated_title: 相同操作，不同权限：评估护栏是否遵循授权
translated_abstract: 随着语言模型智能体代表用户编写代码、转移资金和修改记录，判断某个操作是否获得授权已成为一个核心的安全问题。护栏（guardrails）通常被部署在这些操作之前，但很少有评估工作去检验它们的决策是否真正遵循授权：即在阻止未授权操作的同时，仍然允许在有效权限下执行相同的操作。我们提出了 \bench{}，这是一个在其语言轨道上针对同一操作对比授权证据的基准。它将专家标注的自然语言场景与经过实际执行和验证的操作相结合，并包含来自外部来源的原生策略请求。\bench{} 会检查每个决策的正确性、可用性及其产生的效果，并在护栏变更的过程中跟踪每个请求的表现。我们的实验表明，许多被阻止的操作源于评审失败，而非正确的拒绝。修复输出格式可以恢复可用的决策，但会改变哪些操作被授权……
tldr: 该论文提出了 \bench{} 基准，通过对比同一操作在不同授权条件下的决策结果来评估护栏是否正确遵循授权，实验发现许多被阻止的操作源于评审失败而非正确的拒绝，且修复输出格式虽能恢复可用决策却会改变授权结果。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces \bench{}, a benchmark that evaluates whether guardrails honor authorization by contrasting decisions on the same operation under different permissions, showing that many blocked operations stem from failed reviews rather than correct denials, and that repairing output format restores usable decisions but changes which actions get authorized.
